title: NVIDIA Just Bought the Town Square Where AI Is Built — 18 Million Developers and All
subtitle: The chipmaker that sells the shovels of the AI gold rush just agreed to buy Hugging Face, the open-source hub — the GitHub of AI — where 18 million developers pick the models they build on. It's NVIDIA's biggest acquisition ever, and a declaration that open-weights AI is now a moat, not a trend.
summary: NVIDIA agreed on Thursday to acquire Hugging Face, the open-source hub where 18 million developers share and download AI models, in the chipmaker's largest outright acquisition ever. The roughly $12.9 billion deal extends NVIDIA's CUDA moat to the developer layer and doubles down on open-weights AI. Hugging Face stays neutral — no NVIDIA compute required — while US and EU regulators take a long look before a first-half-2027 close.

bodyHtml:
Silicon Valley's central banker just bought the town square. On Thursday, NVIDIA — the company that builds the chips powering most of the world's artificial intelligence — agreed to acquire Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion, the biggest outright acquisition in its history. If you don't follow AI infrastructure daily, here's the two-line version: NVIDIA makes the GPUs nearly every serious AI model is trained on, while Hugging Face is the GitHub of AI — the open-source hub where more than 18 million developers, researchers, and creators share and download open-weight models, browse 3 million-plus models and 500,000 datasets, and ship over a million applications on top of them.

That's the deal math. Here's the story. For two decades, NVIDIA has sold the picks and shovels of every compute gold rush, and the moat has been CUDA, the software that makes its chips sing. This deal reaches one layer higher — to the developers themselves, the people who decide which models get built, which models get used, and therefore how much compute the world needs. More builders means more chips, and NVIDIA just bought the place where the builders gather.

It's also the loudest signal yet in the open-versus-closed model war. Hugging Face is where open-weights AI lives, and open-weights AI is having a moment: NVIDIA runs Nemotron, its own free open-weight model line, and Huang co-authored an open-weights letter that 80-plus companies have signed. Even the recent drama tells the story — when Hugging Face was hacked in August by autonomous agents, CEO Clem Delangue said the company had to rely on open models to defend itself. Closed labs attacking the open hub; the open hub answering with open tools. NVIDIA just picked a side.

The neutrality promises came fast. 'Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem,' Huang wrote on NVIDIA's blog. Developers keep choosing their own models, frameworks, clouds, inference providers, and compute — NVIDIA compute will not be required. The team stays, the 🤗 brand stays, and Delangue, who initiated the conversation, stays. That's the reassurance the 200,000-plus companies building on Hugging Face needed to hear, because the moment a hub looks like it exists to sell its owner's chips, the developers scatter.

None of this happened overnight. Hugging Face was founded in 2016 by Delangue, Julien Chaumond, and Thomas Wolf, raised more than $400 million along the way, and hit a private valuation of $4.5 billion in 2023 on a Salesforce Ventures-led round, with roughly $150 million in annualized revenue. The $12.9 billion price is about three times that last private mark — a premium that says NVIDIA isn't buying revenue, it's buying gravity. It helps that NVIDIA has long been Hugging Face's biggest contributor of open models and datasets, with more than 500 models and 250-plus open datasets to its name. Buying the bazaar you already supply is the natural next step.

Make no mistake about the size of this: it's NVIDIA's biggest outright acquisition ever, second on record only to the roughly $20 billion Groq asset purchase in December 2025 and far past the $7 billion Mellanox deal of 2019. The company can pay for it almost out of pocket change. In late August it reported a record $96.2 billion in quarterly revenue, up 106 percent year over year, with data-center revenue of $89 billion and GAAP net income of $59.7 billion. Trailing-twelve-month revenue is around $303 billion, the current-quarter guide sits at roughly $108 billion, current assets top $197 billion, and NVIDIA has already sunk some $50 billion into AI labs. It doesn't need this deal for the money. It needs it for the position.

Now the hard part: getting it closed. The deal is expected to land in the first half of 2027, and before that, antitrust reviewers in Washington and Brussels will take a long look. The worry isn't market share, it's neutrality — when the biggest chipmaker in history owns the town square where models get picked, rivals will ask whether the square stays fair. NVIDIA's answer is on the record, and shares ticked up on the news. The market's read: a company that keeps finding ways to extend its lead.

The bottom line: NVIDIA already owns the compute layer of the AI boom. With Hugging Face, it's reaching for the community layer — the place where the next generation of models gets chosen, shared, and built. If open weights keep winning, NVIDIA gets paid twice, once for the chips and once for being the platform everyone trusts. That's not a quarter's story. That's a decade's positioning.

Disclosure: The Signal holds no position in NVDA. Positions may change. This is not financial advice.
